title: Stored Procedures Tutorial
description: Overview of the stored procedures tutorial series covering parameters, variables, control flow, and error handling.

data.text: This tutorial series introduces you to stored procedures and shows you how to develop flexible stored procedures to optimize database access. SQL Server stored procedures are used to group one or more Transact-SQL statements into logical units.

items: Basic guide to stored procedures — create, execute, modify, and drop.
Parameters — create stored procedures with input and optional parameters.
Variables — declare and use variables in stored procedures.
Output Parameters — return data from stored procedures using OUTPUT parameters.
IF...ELSE — execute statements based on conditions.
WHILE — loop based on a condition.
RAISERROR and THROW — generate user-defined error messages.
Dynamic SQL — construct flexible SQL statements at runtime.

data.text: This procedure takes a required customer id and an optional start date, then returns that customer's orders. Defaults make the second parameter optional at the call site.

data.title: Create and execute a stored procedure
data.content: `CREATE OR ALTER` is available from SQL Server 2016 SP1 onward and is safer than dropping and recreating the procedure.

data.title: Procedures cache a plan
data.text: SQL Server compiles and caches a plan the first time a procedure runs, which is why procedures can be fast — and why the same plan can be bad for a different parameter value (parameter sniffing). See the parameter-sniffing lesson for `OPTION (RECOMPILE)` and plan-guide strategies.

data.title: Stored Procedures Tutorial Key Points
points: Stored procedures group T-SQL into reusable logical units.
The tutorial series covers basics, parameters, variables, and advanced topics.
Control-of-flow statements enable complex logic within procedures.
Error handling and dynamic SQL provide flexibility and robustness.
